comment: Seeds are plate ids with the NAME the model's own continental-polygon file gives them; build_chapters.py asserts each name. Every other plate id joins the group of its nearest seed (great-circle distance between polygons), if within maxDistanceKm. A hidden group absorbs its neighbours and is then left out of the set.

notes: Italy, Greece and Anatolia are seeded into Eurasia: in the model they are small blocks touching both Africa (Sicily is part of plate 715) and Europe, so which one they join is a teaching choice, made here for the continent a student would expect.
Chukotka, Kolyma and Omolon are seeded into Eurasia (the model puts them on North America).

Dropped: island arcs (GPGIM_TYPE), crust the model says appeared after minAppearanceMa, and the LIPs listed in drop. The LIP list is explicit: EarthByte's LIP outlines (2012) also cover the Seychelles, Danakil and the Batavia/Gulden Draak knolls, which are continental fragments, so the overlap is reported by the build but never used to drop anything.

keep overrides the appearance-age rule for orogenic belts inside continents (Alps-Carpathians, Dinarides, Serbo-Macedonia, Romeral): the model gives them young appearance ages because they sit in deforming belts, not because the crust is new, and dropping them punches holes in Europe and the Andes.

SE Asia: the model's blocks touch in a chain from New Guinea to Luzon, so ties decide where growth sends them. Both sides are seeded explicitly: West, SW and NE Sulawesi, Sumba, the Philippines and Luzon into Eurasia; Bird's Head, Timor, Seram, Sula-Banggai, SE Sulawesi and Obi into Australia. Halmahera is left to growth. A teaching simplification, not a claim about origins.

shelves: the blocks set with Zealandia shown: Lord Howe Rise, Challenger Plateau, Campbell Plateau (including Chatham Rise, which the model draws as part of plate 813's 'Eastern Province' polygon) and the New Zealand islands. Norfolk Ridge, New Caledonia and Three Kings Rise are dropped by minAppearanceMa (the model dates them 50 Ma).
